ai.description: This 8–10 cm lizard is brownish-grey with a pale throat and dark cross-bands. It features a prominent, fleshy gular pouch and highly mobile, kangaroo-like hind limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the presence of a distinct, elongated gular pouch (throat fan) in males, which is absent or significantly reduced in other similar agamid species.
ai.habitat: *Agasthyagama beddomii* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen shola forests and moist deciduous woodlands of the southern Western Ghats, typically above 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indian Kangaroo Lizard is primarily diurnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by standing on its hind legs to sprint away when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Agasthyagama beddomii* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 1–2 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from May to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Agasthyagama beddomii* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, primarily occurring in Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 600 and 1,600 meters.
